symbols.name: scalar ring
symbols.meaning: The ring the network's scalars and gate coefficients lie in, F_2 for the bit network and Z[i,1/2] for the complex one.
symbols.quote: Replace each scalar of the [linear exchange network](linear-network.md) by an array in $R^\Omega$, where $R$ is the scalar ring and $\Omega$ a finite address set shared by all wires, and apply each gate at every address; call the result $\mathsf S_\Omega$.

symbols.name: address set
symbols.meaning: The finite set of addresses, shared by all wires, that indexes the entries of each wire's array.
symbols.quote: Replace each scalar of the [linear exchange network](linear-network.md) by an array in $R^\Omega$, where $R$ is the scalar ring and $\Omega$ a finite address set shared by all wires, and apply each gate at every address; call the result $\mathsf S_\Omega$.

symbols.name: array network
symbols.meaning: The network obtained by applying each scalar gate at every address, acting on the vector of all wire arrays.
symbols.quote: Replace each scalar of the [linear exchange network](linear-network.md) by an array in $R^\Omega$, where $R$ is the scalar ring and $\Omega$ a finite address set shared by all wires, and apply each gate at every address; call the result $\mathsf S_\Omega$.

symbols.name: vertex
symbols.meaning: A vertex of a wire: its source, a gate on it, or its sink.
symbols.quote: At each vertex $v$ (source, gate or sink) choose an invertible $R$-linear frame $D_v$ on $R^\Omega$; unlike a gate, it may mix addresses.

symbols.name: frame
symbols.meaning: The invertible R-linear operator on R^Omega chosen at vertex v, so that the stored array there is D_v applied to the logical array.
symbols.quote: At each vertex $v$ (source, gate or sink) choose an invertible $R$-linear frame $D_v$ on $R^\Omega$; unlike a gate, it may mix addresses.

symbols.name: edge start vertex
symbols.meaning: The vertex at the start of an edge whose end is v.
symbols.quote: All wires at a gate share its frame; an edge from $u$ to $v$ applies the change of frame $D_vD_u^{-1}$.

symbols.name: role
symbols.meaning: A role, the fixed name of a wire in the network.
symbols.quote: $D_{\rm in}$ applies $D_{\mathrm{source}(w)}$ to the input array on each role $w$; $D_{\rm out}$ applies $D_{\mathrm{sink}(w)}$ to each output.

symbols.name: input frame operator
symbols.meaning: The operator applying the source frame of each input role to that role's array.
symbols.quote: $D_{\rm in}$ applies $D_{\mathrm{source}(w)}$ to the input array on each role $w$; $D_{\rm out}$ applies $D_{\mathrm{sink}(w)}$ to each output.

symbols.name: output frame operator
symbols.meaning: The operator applying the sink frame of each output role to that role's array.
symbols.quote: $D_{\rm in}$ applies $D_{\mathrm{source}(w)}$ to the input array on each role $w$; $D_{\rm out}$ applies $D_{\mathrm{sink}(w)}$ to each output.

symbols.name: physical input
symbols.meaning: The vector of input arrays actually supplied to the machine.
symbols.quote: Read a physical input $f$ as the logical input $g=D_{\rm in}^{-1}f$; no work is done.

symbols.name: logical input
symbols.meaning: The logical input D_in^{-1} f, the arrays the stored input represents.
symbols.quote: Read a physical input $f$ as the logical input $g=D_{\rm in}^{-1}f$; no work is done.

symbols.name: edge logical array
symbols.meaning: The logical array carried by a wire along one edge.
symbols.quote: An edge carrying logical array $\varphi$ turns stored $D_u\varphi$ into $D_v\varphi$.

symbols.name: gate logical input
symbols.meaning: The logical array on the j-th wire entering a gate.
symbols.quote: A gate outputs combinations $\sum_jc_j\varphi_j$ of its logical inputs $\varphi_j$, with coefficients $c_j\in R$ equal at every address, so by linearity $\sum_jc_jD_v\varphi_j=D_v\sum_jc_j\varphi_j$: the shared frame commutes with the gate.

symbols.name: gate coefficient
symbols.meaning: The coefficient in R with which a gate output combines its j-th input, the same at every address.
symbols.quote: A gate outputs combinations $\sum_jc_j\varphi_j$ of its logical inputs $\varphi_j$, with coefficients $c_j\in R$ equal at every address, so by linearity $\sum_jc_jD_v\varphi_j=D_v\sum_jc_j\varphi_j$: the shared frame commutes with the gate.

symbols.name: role permutation
symbols.meaning: The permutation of roles sending each input role to its output role, swapping the two banks and fixing scratch roles.
symbols.quote: The exchange network sends input role $w$ to output role $\rho(w)$ with sign $\varepsilon_w=\pm1$, where $\rho$ swaps the two banks and fixes every scratch role.

symbols.name: route sign
symbols.meaning: The sign, plus or minus one, that the exchange network attaches to the value on input role w.
symbols.quote: The exchange network sends input role $w$ to output role $\rho(w)$ with sign $\varepsilon_w=\pm1$, where $\rho$ swaps the two banks and fixes every scratch role.

symbols.name: role logical array
symbols.meaning: The part of the logical input g on input role w.
symbols.quote: So $\mathsf S_\Omega$ moves the logical array $g_w$ of $w$ to role $\rho(w)$ as $\varepsilon_wg_w$, and the route from $w$ applies $\varepsilon_wD_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))}D_{\mathrm{source}(w)}^{-1}$ to its input array, scratch roles included.

symbols.name: consecutive wire vertices
symbols.meaning: Three consecutive vertices along one wire.
symbols.quote: Interior frames cancel because edge changes telescope, $(D_{v_2}D_{v_1}^{-1})(D_{v_1}D_{v_0}^{-1})=D_{v_2}D_{v_0}^{-1}$ for consecutive vertices $v_0,v_1,v_2$ on a wire, and gates let their frame through; they only set edge costs.

symbols.name: first address chunk
symbols.meaning: The address chunk of m fields that the bit-procedure frames shift.
symbols.quote: In the bit procedure, addresses contain two chunks $h,d$ of $m$ fields each; vertex $v$ gets a rational $m\times m$ matrix $M_v$ and the frame $\Phi_{M_v}$ moving the entry at $(h,d)$ to $(h+M_vd,\,d)$.

symbols.name: second address chunk
symbols.meaning: The address chunk of m fields by which the bit-procedure frames shift h.
symbols.quote: In the bit procedure, addresses contain two chunks $h,d$ of $m$ fields each; vertex $v$ gets a rational $m\times m$ matrix $M_v$ and the frame $\Phi_{M_v}$ moving the entry at $(h,d)$ to $(h+M_vd,\,d)$.

symbols.name: fields per chunk
symbols.meaning: The number of address fields in each of the chunks h and d.
symbols.quote: In the bit procedure, addresses contain two chunks $h,d$ of $m$ fields each; vertex $v$ gets a rational $m\times m$ matrix $M_v$ and the frame $\Phi_{M_v}$ moving the entry at $(h,d)$ to $(h+M_vd,\,d)$.

symbols.name: frame matrix
symbols.meaning: The fixed rational m by m matrix attached to vertex v in the bit procedure.
symbols.quote: In the bit procedure, addresses contain two chunks $h,d$ of $m$ fields each; vertex $v$ gets a rational $m\times m$ matrix $M_v$ and the frame $\Phi_{M_v}$ moving the entry at $(h,d)$ to $(h+M_vd,\,d)$.

symbols.name: shear frame
symbols.meaning: The frame moving the array entry at (h,d) to (h + M_v d, d).
symbols.quote: In the bit procedure, addresses contain two chunks $h,d$ of $m$ fields each; vertex $v$ gets a rational $m\times m$ matrix $M_v$ and the frame $\Phi_{M_v}$ moving the entry at $(h,d)$ to $(h+M_vd,\,d)$.
